system:
You are a medicinal chemist advising a hit-to-lead optimisation campaign.

You will be shown compounds from a congeneric series with their measured
potencies, and a numbered menu of substructures that occur in the virtual
library. Your job is to state a structural hypothesis about what makes a
compound potent in this series, as a constraint that will narrow the library.

You choose substructures by their menu index. You do not write SMARTS.

Guidance:
- Aim to keep roughly 5-25% of the library. Each menu entry shows how much of
  the library it matches; requiring two entries keeps at most the smaller.
- Prefer one or two well-chosen entries. Requiring many at once usually matches
  nothing, which wastes the constraint entirely.
- Only state a descriptor range if the data supports it. Use a wide range when
  you mean "unbounded on this side".
- You are choosing what to *explore*, not predicting individual values. A
  constraint that excludes the best compound is far worse than one that is
  slightly too permissive.

Respond with JSON only.

response.hypothesis: The top 10 compounds (pchembl > 8.5) all share a specific scaffold where the pyridine ring is attached via an ether linkage to a phenyl ring bearing a fluorine and a chlorine, which is then connected to the core via an amine or ether bridge. Specifically, the high potency correlates with the presence of the 'methoxy' group on the core (substructure [2]) combined with the 'fluorine' substituent on the distal aromatic ring (substructure [1]). Compounds lacking the methoxy group on the core (e.g., the acrylamide derivatives or the sulfone analogs) drop significantly in potency (pchembl < 8.0). Furthermore, the most potent compounds (9.52, 9.31, 9.16) all contain the methoxy group and a fluorine atom on the distal ring, whereas the lowest potency compounds often lack one or both of these features or possess reactive Michael acceptors which may reduce affinity or increase off-target effects. Therefore, we should constrain the library to retain the methoxy group on the core scaffold and the fluorine atom on the distal aromatic ring.
